steps: Headline and within-month change: analyst.daily_stats for 13 and 14 Nov 2026, the only refresh days between 1 Nov and 1 Dec 2026, because collection started on 12 Nov 2026.

Demand, employers, automation, skills and tools: a snapshot of analyst.jobs as at 14 Nov 2026 (3,706 ads posted 16 Sep–14 Nov and still open in the 60-day window), joined to analyst.job_skills, analyst.job_tools, analyst.employers and analyst.employer_ratings (salary benchmark).
Pay: analyst.salary_benchmarks (salary benchmark, national) compared with the median of salary_annual/12 in analyst.jobs where salary_imputed = false (530 ads), for families with 15 or more such ads.
Look-back: analyst.search_interest, term groups 'jobs: job seeking · 12 months' and 'jobs: work style · 12 months', using weekly values from 1 Jun to 8 Nov 2026 averaged per month and term.
Automatable value = salary × 1.25 × automation score / 100, summed per role family.
trust: Role, province and employer counts come directly from 3,706 ads, refreshed daily.
The salary benchmark benchmarks used carry VERY_HIGH confidence, with 37 to 741 salaries per title.
Search patterns from Jun to Oct 2026 rest on 4–5 weekly points per month.
limits: There is no ad data before 12 Nov 2026; earlier months are covered only by search-trend data, never by ad counts.
86% of ad salaries are imputed and published salaries skew senior (37% vs 29%); the compliance-officer benchmark appears to be annual and was excluded.
November search interest covers 1–8 Nov only, and tool and skill mentions are under-counted in short ads.

risks: Only two collection days (13–14 Nov) exist, so there is no reliable within-month trend or prior-month comparison yet.
86% of ad salaries are imputed, so the automatable rand values are estimates.
Tool and skill mentions are under-counted: only 12% of third-party job-ad providers name a tool.

actions: 1. Lock 14 Nov (3,706 roles) as the baseline and report the December pack as month-on-month change against it.
2. Reset offer bands for admin and finance roles to salary benchmark P50–P75 (creditors clerk R15.0k–R18.0k, payroll administrator R18.5k–R24.0k a month).
3. Before backfilling, review every Data Capture, Creditors & Debtors and Call Centre vacancy for automation redesign (R113m of automatable work across these three families).
4. Launch a training track on Sage Pastel, Excel reconciliations and reporting, with eFiling (SARS) as an add-on.
5. Post seasonal, part-time and remote admin roles in the next 2–3 weeks, while search interest is at its six-month high.
6. Negotiate volume terms with agencies for logistics and data-capture hiring (64% and 63% agency share), and track whether the 45% agency share moves.
findings: The November baseline is 3,706 open roles (14 Nov), split evenly between direct employers (45%) and recruitment agencies (45%).
Demand concentrates in Office Admin (562), Creditors & Debtors (371), Call Centre (357) and Logistics (351), and 55% of ads are in Gauteng plus the Western Cape.
JVR Software posts 11% of direct ads; the top 10 direct employers post 23%; rated big hirers average 3.5 on salary benchmark.
Advertised salaries overstate market pay by 13–213% because ads that publish pay skew senior; salary benchmark medians are the better anchor.
R419m a year of work is automatable: three families hold 43%, and Data Capture is the most exposed (score 85).
Candidate interest is moving to part-time work (+142% since August) and remote work (a six-month high) ahead of the festive season.
